issues.description: The template Lecture class defines addGuestStudents with signature addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) which conflicts with the problem statement and the solution. The specification and UML expect addGuestStudents(int): void, and the solution implements addGuestStudents(int). This mismatch will confuse students and prevent them from implementing the method as specified or matching the solution/tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature to match the specification: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { /* TODO */ }. Alternatively, provide an overloaded method (both addGuestStudents(int) and addGuestStudents(int, boolean)) and clearly document the intended primary signature so students can implement the required method.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML require an addGuestStudents(int) method (single int parameter), and the provided solution implements addGuestStudents(int). However, the template's Lecture.java declares addGuestStudents with a different signature: addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput). This mismatch in the method signature (extra boolean parameter) creates a mapping barrier: students following the task/UML may implement or expect addGuestStudents(int), while the template enforces a different method shape, causing confusion and potential test/compilation failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the problem statement and solution by changing the template method signature to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) (remove the boolean parameter). Alternatively, update the problem statement and UML to reflect the two-parameter version if the boolean validation flag is intentional. Prefer removing the extra parameter to match the existing UML and solution.
